name: OPEC and non-OPEC output cut
trigger: OPEC and independent oil exporters meeting in Vienna approve a withdrawal of about 2.1 million barrels per day from the oil market.
source_quote: Venezuela’s energy minister, Ali Rodriguez stated the withdrawal of 2.104 billion barrels per day from the oil market, approved by OPEC and independent exporters in Vienna Tuesday, will pick up prices and the slumped economy.

name: US-China bilateral WTO accession deal
trigger: The United States and China complete bilateral talks on China's accession to the World Trade Organization.
source_quote: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and National Economic Council Director Gene Sperling today announced the successful completion of bilateral talks on China's accession to the World Trade Organization.

name: AOL and Time Warner merger announced
trigger: America Online and Time Warner announce that they plan to merge, combining an internet company with a media conglomerate.
source_quote: Internet giant America Online (AOL) and media conglomerate Time Warner have announced that they plan to merge.

name: Microsoft antitrust settlement talks collapse
trigger: Mediated antitrust settlement talks between Microsoft and the US government end in failure after four months, leaving a court ruling pending.
source_quote: The mediator in the Microsoft case said on Saturday that four months of settlement talks had ended in failure.

name: Fed raises rates by 50 basis points
trigger: The Federal Reserve raises its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points.
source_quote: The Federal Open Market Committee voted today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 6-1/2 percent.

name: Intel third-quarter revenue warning
trigger: Intel warns after the close that third-quarter revenue will be below its previous expectations, mainly because of weaker demand in Europe.
source_quote: Intel's third quarter revenue is anticipated to be below the company's previous expectations, primarily due to weaker demand in Europe, the company said today.

name: Strategic Petroleum Reserve oil exchange
trigger: President Clinton directs the Energy Secretary to exchange 30 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve over 30 days.
source_quote: Yesterday I directed the Secretary of Energy to exchange 30 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve over the next 30 days.

name: US presidential election left undecided
trigger: The US presidential election is undecided after Al Gore withdraws his concession and the result depends on a recount in Florida.
source_quote: The race for the United States presidency remains undecided after a night of drama, with the result depending on a recount being carried out in the state of Florida.

name: Gore concedes the 2000 election
trigger: Al Gore concedes the presidential election to George W Bush after a Supreme Court decision ends the Florida recounts.
source_quote: Vice-President Al Gore conceded defeat on Wednesday night, ending the longest and most complex US presidential election in well over a century.

name: Fed surprise intermeeting rate cut
trigger: The Federal Reserve lowers its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points in an unscheduled decision between meetings.
source_quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 6 percent.

name: Microsoft breakup order overturned
trigger: A US appeals court overturns the ruling that Microsoft must be broken up.
source_quote: A US appeals court has overturned a ruling that software giant Microsoft must be broken up.

name: September 11 attacks
trigger: Hijackers fly airliners into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon, killing thousands; US stock exchanges reopen for the first time since the attacks.
source_quote: The United States is in a state of shock after a day of attacks which have left thousands dead and New York's World Trade Center destroyed.

name: Fed rate cut after September 11
trigger: The Federal Reserve lowers its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points following the September 11 attacks.
source_quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 3 percent.

name: US military campaign in Afghanistan begins
trigger: The United States begins Operation Enduring Freedom, a military campaign against al-Qaeda and the Taleban in Afghanistan.
source_quote: The United States has begun its military campaign, Operation Enduring Freedom, against al-Qaeda and the Taleban in Afghanistan.

name: WTO approves China's accession
trigger: The members of the World Trade Organisation unanimously approve China's accession to membership.
source_quote: In a ceremony lasting just a few minutes, the 142 members of the World Trade Organisation unanimously approved the accession of the world's largest country into membership.

name: Enron bankruptcy filing
trigger: Energy trader Enron files for bankruptcy protection under the burden of about $16bn of debt.
source_quote: Energy giant Enron has announced that it has filed for bankruptcy protection as it struggles under the burden of a $16bn debt.

name: Argentina suspends foreign debt payments
trigger: Argentina's newly installed interim president announces that the country will suspend payments on its foreign debt.
source_quote: Argentina's newly installed interim president has announced the country will suspend its foreign debt payments, triggering the biggest debt default in history.

name: WorldCom bankruptcy filing
trigger: WorldCom files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection from its creditors while it tries to restructure.
source_quote: The firm went into Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Monday morning, a process which protects it from its creditors while it tries to restructure.

name: Bali nightclub bombing
trigger: A car bomb explodes outside a crowded nightclub on the Indonesian holiday island of Bali, killing scores of people.
source_quote: At least 182 people are now known to have died in a devastating car bomb blast outside a crowded nightclub on the Indonesian holiday island of Bali.

name: WHO global alert on atypical pneumonia (SARS)
trigger: The WHO issues a global alert about outbreaks of a severe form of atypical pneumonia in Viet Nam, Hong Kong and Guangdong province.
source_quote: Since mid February, WHO has been actively working to confirm reports of outbreaks of a severe form of pneumonia in Viet Nam, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR), China, and Guangdong province in China.

name: Iraq war begins
trigger: US President George W Bush launches war on Iraq with strikes on Baghdad.
source_quote: US President George W Bush has launched war on Baghdad, vowing to "disarm Iraq and to free its people".

name: WHO declares SARS outbreak contained
trigger: The WHO says human chains of SARS virus transmission appear to have been broken everywhere in the world.
source_quote: Based on country surveillance reports, the human chains of SARS virus transmission appear to have been broken everywhere in the world.

name: Northeast US and Canada blackout
trigger: A spreading power failure blacks out large areas from New York to Detroit and from Toronto to Ottawa.
source_quote: The power failures caused chaos as they spread from New York to Detroit, and Toronto to Ottawa.

name: Istanbul consulate and HSBC bombings
trigger: Bomb attacks hit the British consulate and the HSBC bank headquarters in Istanbul, killing dozens.
source_quote: Bomb attacks on the British consulate and the HSBC bank headquarters in Istanbul have left at least 27 dead and up to 400 injured.

name: US steel tariffs repealed
trigger: President George W Bush repeals US tariffs on imported steel to avoid a damaging trade war.
source_quote: President George W Bush has repealed US tariffs on imported steel to avoid a damaging trade war.

name: Madrid train bombings
trigger: Explosions tear through three Madrid train stations during the morning rush hour, killing at least 170 people.
source_quote: At least 170 people have died and 500 have been injured as huge explosions tore through three Madrid train stations during the morning rush-hour.

name: Fed raises rates by 25 basis points
trigger: The Federal Reserve raises its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points.
source_quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/4 percent.

name: Google IPO
trigger: Google begins trading on the Nasdaq after selling shares at $85 each through a Dutch auction.
source_quote: Google shares - whose offer price had been set at $85 - ended their market debut up $15.33 at $100.33.

name: Kerry concedes, Bush wins second term
trigger: John Kerry concedes defeat and George W Bush declares victory in the US presidential election.
source_quote: George W Bush has declared victory in the US presidential election after his Democratic challenger John Kerry admitted defeat.

name: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
trigger: An earthquake under the Indian Ocean triggers sea surges that kill thousands of people across southern Asia.
source_quote: Massive sea surges triggered by an earthquake under the Indian Ocean have killed over 10,000 people in southern Asia, with many more feared dead.

name: London transport bombings
trigger: A series of bomb attacks on London's transport network kills dozens and injures hundreds.
source_quote: A series of bomb attacks on London's transport network has killed more than 30 people and injured about 700 others.

name: China revalues the yuan
trigger: China revalues the yuan for the first time in a decade, a move welcomed by the US, a long-time critic of its exchange-rate policy.
source_quote: China has revalued its currency, the yuan, for the first time in a decade - a move welcomed by the US, a long-time critic of its exchange-rate policy.

name: Hurricane Katrina landfall
trigger: Hurricane Katrina sweeps ashore on the southern Louisiana coast and pounds New Orleans with high winds and heavy rain.
source_quote: Hurricane Katrina is pummelling New Orleans with howling gusts and blinding rain, after sweeping ashore over the southern Louisiana coast.

name: H5N1 bird flu confirmed in Turkey
trigger: Bird flu found in Turkey is confirmed as the H5N1 strain dangerous to humans, and EU states are urged to stockpile antiviral drugs.
source_quote: EU states have been urged to stockpile anti-viral drugs after confirmation that the bird flu virus found in Turkey is the H5N1 strain dangerous to humans.

name: Israel-Lebanon war begins
trigger: Lebanese guerrillas capture two Israeli soldiers in a cross-border raid, and Israel sends ground forces into Lebanon.
source_quote: Lebanese guerrillas have captured two Israeli soldiers in a cross-border raid, triggering the first Israeli land incursion into the country since 2000.

name: UK transatlantic airline bomb plot disrupted
trigger: UK police say they have disrupted a plot to blow up flights from the UK to the US, and searches take place across England.
source_quote: Homes and businesses across England are being searched and 24 people questioned after police say a plot to blow up UK flights to the US was disrupted.

name: North Korea nuclear test
trigger: North Korea announces it has carried out an underground nuclear test in defiance of international warnings.
source_quote: It said the underground test, carried out in defiance of international warnings, was a success and had not resulted in any leak of radiation.

name: Apple unveils the iPhone
trigger: Apple introduces the iPhone, combining a mobile phone, a widescreen iPod with touch controls and an internet communications device.
source_quote: Apple® today introduced iPhone, combining three products—a revolutionary mobile phone, a widescreen iPod® with touch controls, and a breakthrough Internet communications device with desktop-class email, web browsing, searching and maps—into one small and lightweight handheld device.

name: BNP Paribas suspends subprime-exposed funds
trigger: BNP Paribas suspends three investment funds, citing problems in the US sub-prime mortgage sector.
source_quote: This came after French bank BNP Paribas suspended three investment funds worth 2bn euros (£1.35bn), citing problems in the US sub-prime mortgage sector.

name: Fed cuts the discount rate
trigger: The Federal Reserve cuts the primary credit discount rate by 50 basis points to promote orderly conditions in financial markets.
source_quote: To promote the restoration of orderly conditions in financial markets, the Federal Reserve Board approved temporary changes to its primary credit discount window facility. The Board approved a 50 basis point reduction in the primary credit rate to 5-3/4 percent, to narrow the spread between the primary credit rate and the Federal Open Market Committee's target federal funds rate to 50 basis points.

name: Fed emergency 75 basis point cut
trigger: The Federal Reserve lowers its target for the federal funds rate by 75 basis points in an unscheduled decision.
source_quote: The Federal Open Market Committee has decided to lower its target for the federal funds rate 75 basis points to 3-1/2 percent.

name: JPMorgan acquires Bear Stearns with Fed financing
trigger: JPMorgan Chase agrees to acquire Bear Stearns, and the Federal Reserve approves a financing arrangement for the deal.
source_quote: The Board also approved the financing arrangement announced by JPMorgan Chase & Co. and The Bear Stearns Companies Inc.

name: Russia-Georgia war
trigger: Russian tanks enter Georgia's breakaway region of South Ossetia, according to Georgia's president.
source_quote: Russian tanks have entered Georgia's breakaway region of South Ossetia, says Georgian President Mikhail Saakashvili.

name: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac placed in conservatorship
trigger: The FHFA places Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac in conservatorship, and the Treasury takes steps to support both enterprises.
source_quote: Treasury has taken three additional steps to complement FHFA’s decision to place both enterprises in conservatorship.

name: Lehman Brothers bankruptcy
trigger: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy protection after a weekend of emergency talks on Wall Street.
source_quote: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy protection after a weekend of frantic activity on Wall Street.

name: Federal Reserve loan to AIG
trigger: The Federal Reserve, with Treasury support, authorizes the New York Fed to lend up to $85 billion to AIG.
source_quote: The Federal Reserve Board on Tuesday, with the full support of the Treasury Department, authorized the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to lend up to $85 billion to the American International Group (AIG) under section 13(3) of the Federal Reserve Act.

name: House rejects the $700bn rescue plan
trigger: The US House of Representatives rejects the government's financial rescue plan by 228 votes to 205.
source_quote: The rescue plan, a result of tense talks between the government and lawmakers, was rejected by 228 to 205 votes in the House of Representatives.

name: House passes the $700bn rescue plan
trigger: The US House of Representatives passes the $700bn government plan to rescue the US financial sector.
source_quote: The US House of Representatives has passed a $700bn (£394bn) government plan to rescue the US financial sector.

name: Coordinated central bank rate cuts
trigger: Six central banks, including the Federal Reserve, the ECB and the Bank of England, announce coordinated reductions in policy interest rates.
source_quote: Accordingly, the Bank of Canada, the Bank of England, the European Central Bank, the Federal Reserve, Sveriges Riksbank, and the Swiss National Bank are today announcing reductions in policy interest rates.

name: Fed announces GSE debt and MBS purchases
trigger: The Federal Reserve announces a program to buy direct obligations of Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the Federal Home Loan Banks, and agency mortgage-backed securities.
source_quote: The Federal Reserve announced on Tuesday that it will initiate a program to purchase the direct obligations of housing-related government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs)--Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and the Federal Home Loan Banks--and mortgage-backed securities (MBS) backed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Ginnie Mae.

name: Fed cuts rates to near zero
trigger: The Federal Reserve sets a target range for the federal funds rate just above zero.
source_quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to establish a target range for the federal funds rate of 0 to 1/4 percent.

name: Fed expands asset purchases to Treasuries
trigger: The Federal Reserve decides to buy up to $300 billion of longer-term Treasury securities over six months to improve private credit conditions.
source_quote: Moreover, to help improve conditions in private credit markets, the Committee decided to purchase up to $300 billion of longer-term Treasury securities over the next six months.

name: WHO declares swine flu a health emergency
trigger: The WHO says the swine flu outbreak is a health emergency of international concern that must be closely monitored.
source_quote: Margaret Chan said the outbreak was a "health emergency of international concern" and must be closely monitored.

name: US bank stress test results released
trigger: Federal bank supervisors release the results of a forward-looking assessment of the 19 largest US bank holding companies.
source_quote: The results of a comprehensive, forward-looking assessment of the financial conditions of the nation's 19 largest bank holding companies (BHCs) by the federal bank supervisory agencies were released on Thursday.

name: WHO declares H1N1 pandemic
trigger: The WHO raises its pandemic warning to Phase 6, declaring that the A(H1N1) influenza outbreak has reached global pandemic levels.
source_quote: The A(H1N1) influenza outbreak has officially reached global pandemic levels, the public health arm of the United Nations announced today, as it raised its warning system to Phase 6.

name: US tariffs on Chinese tyres
trigger: Under pressure from US unions, the White House announces additional duties on Chinese-made tyres for three years.
source_quote: On Friday, under pressure from US unions, the White House announced duties of an additional 35% on Chinese-made tyres for one year, followed by tariffs of 30% and 25% in the following two years.

name: FDA approves H1N1 vaccines
trigger: The US Food and Drug Administration approves four vaccines against the 2009 H1N1 influenza virus.
source_quote: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced today that it has approved four vaccines against the 2009 H1N1 influenza virus.

name: Icelandic volcanic ash closes European airspace
trigger: Ash from a volcanic eruption in Iceland suspends all flights in and out of the UK and several other European countries.
source_quote: All flights in and out of the UK and several other European countries have been suspended as ash from a volcanic eruption in Iceland moves south.

name: Deepwater Horizon rig explosion
trigger: The Deepwater Horizon drilling rig explodes and burns in the Gulf of Mexico south-east of the Louisiana coast.
source_quote: The Deepwater Horizon rig was still burning hours after the blast on Tuesday night, 84km (52 miles) south-east of the Louisiana port of Venice.

name: S&P downgrades Greece to junk
trigger: Standard & Poor's cuts Greece's debt rating to below investment grade and lowers Portugal's rating.
source_quote: S&P said it was lowering its rating on Greece's debt to BB+ from BBB-. It also reducing Portugal's debt rating by two notches to A- as doubts intensified about countries with substantial debt relative to GDP.

name: Eurozone-IMF bailout for Greece
trigger: Eurozone members and the IMF agree a 110bn-euro three-year bail-out package for Greece.
source_quote: Eurozone members and the IMF have agreed a 110bn-euro (£95bn; $146.2bn) three-year bail-out package to rescue Greece's embattled economy.

name: May 2010 flash crash
trigger: Liquidity in US equity markets breaks down for several minutes during a day of worry over European sovereign debt, and many stocks trade at extreme prices.
source_quote: On May 6, 2010, the prices of many U.S.-based equity products experienced an extraordinarily rapid decline and recovery.

name: UK hung parliament
trigger: The UK general election produces the first hung parliament since 1974, with the Conservatives the largest party but short of a majority.
source_quote: The Conservatives have won the most MPs in the UK general election but fallen short of a majority, leading to the first hung parliament since 1974.

name: EU 750bn-euro stabilisation package
trigger: European ministers agree emergency measures worth 750bn euros to stop the Greek debt crisis spreading to other eurozone countries.
source_quote: Emergency measures worth 750bn euros ($975bn; £650bn) have been agreed to prevent the Greek debt crisis from affecting other eurozone countries.

name: China pledges a more flexible yuan
trigger: China's central bank announces it will make its exchange rate mechanism more flexible, without details on timing or extent.
source_quote: The Chinese central bank announced it would make its exchange rate mechanism "more flexible", but it gave no details about the timing or extent of changes.

name: Fed announces second round of Treasury purchases (QE2)
trigger: The Federal Reserve announces purchases of a further $600 billion of longer-term Treasury securities at about $75 billion per month.
source_quote: In addition, the Committee intends to purchase a further $600 billion of longer-term Treasury securities by the end of the second quarter of 2011, a pace of about $75 billion per month.

name: North Korea shells Yeonpyeong island
trigger: North Korea fires dozens of artillery shells at a South Korean border island, killing two marines, and the South returns fire.
source_quote: South Korea says it has returned fire after North Korea fired dozens of artillery shells at one of its border islands, killing two marines.

name: Libya unrest shuts oil production
trigger: Unrest in Libya leads European oil companies Repsol and Eni to close down production in the country.
source_quote: Meanwhile, Spanish oil firm Repsol-YFP was joined by Italy's Eni in closing down production in Libya.

name: Japan earthquake and tsunami
trigger: Japan's most powerful recorded earthquake strikes off the north-east coast and triggers a massive tsunami.
source_quote: Japan's most powerful earthquake since records began has struck the north-east coast, triggering a massive tsunami.

name: Osama Bin Laden killed
trigger: President Barack Obama announces that US forces have killed al-Qaeda leader Osama Bin Laden in Pakistan.
source_quote: Al-Qaeda leader Osama Bin Laden has been killed by US forces in Pakistan, President Barack Obama has said.

name: IEA coordinated oil stock release
trigger: The US and its IEA partners decide to release 60 million barrels of oil over 30 days to offset supply lost to unrest in the Middle East.
source_quote: U.S. Energy Secretary Steven Chu announced today that the U.S. and its partners in the International Energy Agency have decided to release a total of 60 million barrels of oil onto the world market over the next 30 days to offset the disruption in the oil supply caused by unrest in the Middle East.

name: US debt ceiling deal
trigger: President Obama announces that leaders of both parties in Congress have reached an agreement to reduce the deficit and avoid a US default.
source_quote: There are still some very important votes to be taken by members of Congress, but I want to announce that the leaders of both parties, in both chambers, have reached an agreement that will reduce the deficit and avoid default

name: S&P downgrades the United States
trigger: Standard & Poor's downgrades the United States' AAA credit rating for the first time.
source_quote: One of the world's leading credit rating agencies, Standard & Poor's, has downgraded the United States' top-notch AAA rating for the first time ever.

name: Thailand floods halt factories
trigger: Floods in central Thailand force Western Digital, Honda Motor and many other companies to suspend production.
source_quote: Western Digital, Honda Motor and many other companies have been forced to suspend production in central Thailand because of the floods.

name: Eurozone summit debt deal
trigger: Eurozone leaders agree that banks take a loss on half the value of their Greek debt, the bailout fund is boosted and banks must raise more capital.
source_quote: They said banks holding Greek debt accepted a 50% loss, the eurozone bailout fund will be boosted and banks will have to raise more capital.

name: EU oil embargo on Iran
trigger: EU foreign ministers formally adopt an oil embargo against Iran over its nuclear programme, banning all new oil contracts with the country.
source_quote: European Union foreign ministers have formally adopted an "unprecedented" oil embargo against Iran over its nuclear programme, banning all new oil contracts with the country.

name: Greek election backs anti-bailout parties
trigger: Two-thirds of Greek voters back parties opposed to the EU/IMF bailout deal, and the largest party falls far short of a majority.
source_quote: Two-thirds of Greek voters backed parties opposed to the EU/IMF deal, renewing fears that Athens may default on its debts and leave the eurozone.

name: Pro-bailout party wins Greek repeat election
trigger: Greece's broadly pro-bailout New Democracy party narrowly wins a repeat election and moves to form a government.
source_quote: World leaders have welcomed the narrow election victory of Greece's broadly pro-bailout New Democracy party and urged Athens to form a cabinet quickly.

name: Draghi: whatever it takes
trigger: ECB President Mario Draghi says that, within its mandate, the ECB is ready to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro.
source_quote: Within our mandate, the ECB is ready to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro. And believe me, it will be enough.

name: Fed open-ended MBS purchases (QE3)
trigger: The Federal Reserve decides to buy additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month to support a stronger recovery.
source_quote: To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with its dual mandate, the Committee agreed today to increase policy accommodation by purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month.
